items.title: Russia Campaigned to Derail Moldova’s Pro-Western Government
items.summary: In Moldova, Moscow paid Orthodox priests, conducted a vote-buying scheme and set up training camps on election interference — all in an effort to derail the Western-leaning government.

items.title: Heat Is Hammering Europe, Again. Here’s What That Looks Like.
items.summary: Extreme temperatures and repeated wildfires are pushing infrastructure to the limit and testing the continent’s resolve.

items.title: The Taliban Kicked the U.S. Out of Afghanistan. Now They Want It Back.
items.summary: In an interview, Afghanistan’s foreign minister called on the U.S. to reopen its embassy and invest in the country — a near-impossible sell for now, analysts and former diplomats say.

items.title: Jason Arday, Cambridge Professor Accused of Plagiarism, Is Found Dead
items.summary: Mr. Arday resigned last week after the university announced an investigation into allegations of plagiarism and fabrication.

items.title: Will Sudan’s El Obeid Become the Next El Fasher? What to Know.
items.summary: Taking El Obeid would allow the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces to consolidate its hold on western Sudan, a significant strategic goal.

items.title: Britain’s Farage Takes a Page From Trump’s Playbook Amid Investigations
items.summary: Nigel Farage, the Reform U.K. leader who resigned from Parliament and won back his seat on Thursday, stays on the offensive and says voters don’t care about allegations of financial impropriety.

items.title: A Prominent Mexican Politician Says U.S. Revoked His Visa

items.title: With Trump’s Hamas Deal in Peril, Kushner Set to Visit Israel for Gaza Talks
items.summary: Jared Kushner, President Trump’s senior aide, is expected to meet with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of Israel, who has rejected a U.S.-backed deal to disarm Hamas.

items.title: Kevin Rideout, American Missionary Kidnapped in Niger, Is Released
items.summary: Kevin Rideout, a pilot, was abducted from his home in the country’s capital, Niamey, last fall. His mission organization said he was in “good health” after his release.

items.title: Farage Wins Special U.K. Election That He Initiated, as Expected
items.summary: Nigel Farage, the leader of Reform U.K., won the Clacton by-election with 63 percent. Count Binface, a novelty candidate, came second with 27 percent, a personal best.

items.title: Hiroshi Okuda, Disrupter Who Revived Toyota in the 1990s, Dies at 93
items.summary: As the car company’s president, he made decisions quickly and shook things up, expanding overseas manufacturing and introducing the Prius, a milestone in automotive history.

items.title: Lawsuit Accuses Selena Gomez of Defrauding Investors in Mental Health Site
items.summary: The actor, singer and beauty mogul founded Wondermind, a mental health platform, with her mother. Investors put in more than $1 million in the venture, which “quietly collapsed,” the suit said.

items.title: Google Turns On Gemini A.I. for Students Using Its Classroom App
items.summary: Google enabled A.I. features for K-12 schools that have allowed student access to Gemini. Until this week, Google automatically enabled Gemini in Classroom only for students 18 or older.
